name: Host Log Forensics
objective: Perform read-only forensic reconstruction from host logs after suspected compromise, identifying attacker traces, persistence, credential use, execution, privilege activity, lateral movement and evidence tampering while preserving provenance and uncertainty.
method: establish evidence provenance, host identity, clock assumptions and analysis window
construct a host-centric event timeline before interpreting intent
identify unusual logons, privilege changes, process ancestry and script execution
trace persistence mechanisms through services, scheduled tasks, registry, WMI and startup-related evidence when logged
trace credential access and credential reuse indicators without assuming credential theft from authentication alone
correlate host execution with outbound and lateral network connections
search for defense-evasion and log-clearing/tampering indicators and record resulting visibility gaps
map evidence-supported behavior to reviewed ATT&CK references when useful
distinguish observed artifacts from forensic hypotheses
emit compromise scope and likely sequence only to the depth supported by evidence
stop_conditions: required host logs are absent or provenance cannot be established
clock/timestamp inconsistency prevents a defensible timeline
evidence does not distinguish malicious activity from expected administration
a conclusion would require disk/memory artifacts that are not available in the current log-only scope
